title: 11. Le grand chamboulement du statut social
gist: A hedge-fund worker feels miserable because friends in AI are getting richer faster than him — an example of what The Economist's Schumpeter column calls “status death,” as capitalism's usual ways of ranking people get disrupted. Luxury brands like LVMH and Ferrari are losing their shine because they became too accessible, banks use elaborate fake titles to soften status loss, Silicon Valley workers fear AI will make them obsolete, and even Donald Trump will eventually face his own demotion when he leaves office. The one silver lining: fear of losing status pushes people to quit and try something new.

body.fr: Les gens adorent comparer leur {{statut|status}} avec celui des autres.

bd.meaning: People love comparing their status with other people's.
chunks: with that of others (celui = 'the one', stands in for 'statut')
bd.key: “celui” replaces a noun to avoid repeating it: celui des autres = “that of others,” instead of saying “le statut des autres” again.

body.fr: Même les {{patrons|bosses}} des grandes entreprises passent du temps sur LinkedIn pour montrer leurs succès.

bd.meaning: Even the bosses of big companies spend time on LinkedIn to show off their successes.
chunks: of big companies (grandes before the noun)
to show their successes (pour + plain verb)
bd.key: pour + plain verb, once more. pour montrer = “to show” — the same “in order to” shape you've seen before.

body.fr: Aujourd'hui, beaucoup de gens vivent ce qu'on appelle {{« la mort du statut »|"status death"}}.

bd.meaning: Today, many people experience what's called 'status death.'
chunks: what people call (ce que + on appelle)
bd.key: “ce que” + on + verb = “what people ___.” ce qu'on appelle = “what is called” — a handy way to introduce a term.

body.fr: Un jeune {{banquier|banker}} très riche est triste parce que ses amis, qui travaillent dans l'intelligence artificielle, gagnent encore plus d'argent que lui.

bd.meaning: A very rich young banker is sad because his friends, who work in AI, earn even more money than him.
chunks: Un jeune banquier très riche est triste
a very rich young banker is sad
gagnent encore plus d'argent que lui
earn even more money than him
bd.key: “que lui” for comparison after a pronoun. After plus … que, “him” becomes the standalone form lui, not “il.”

body.fr: Les marques de luxe connaissent le même problème.

bd.meaning: Luxury brands face the same problem.
bd.key: “même” before the noun = “the same.” le même problème = “the same problem” — don't confuse with même meaning “even,” which turns up elsewhere.

body.fr: Les {{sacs à main|handbags}} de LVMH et de Kering, deux grandes entreprises françaises, se vendent moins bien.

bd.meaning: Handbags from LVMH and Kering, two big French companies, are selling less well.
chunks: Les sacs à main de LVMH et de Kering
sell (se vendre = 'to sell' in the sense of 'to be sold')
bd.key: “se vendre” = “to sell” (be sold). French often uses this reflexive shape for “X sells well/badly,” where English just says “sells.”

body.fr: Pendant longtemps, ces marques ont vendu leurs produits à trop de gens, alors elles ont perdu {{leur image exclusive|their exclusive image}}.

bd.meaning: For a long time, these brands sold their products to too many people, so they lost their exclusive image.
chunks: ces marques ont vendu leurs produits
alors elles ont perdu leur image exclusive
so they lost their exclusive image
bd.key: Past = avoir + past participle, twice in one sentence. ont vendu and ont perdu both follow the same “avoir + past form” pattern.

body.fr: Les voitures électriques chinoises, moins chères, ont {{cassé|broken, shattered}} l'image exclusive du secteur automobile de luxe.

bd.meaning: Cheaper Chinese electric cars have shattered the exclusive image of the luxury car sector.
chunks: l'image exclusive du secteur automobile de luxe
the exclusive image of the luxury car sector
bd.key: moins + adjective, reused. moins chères = “cheaper” — same comparative shape as moins cher from an earlier story, here feminine plural to agree with “voitures.”

body.fr: À cause de ça, les clients ont mal réagi à la première voiture électrique de Ferrari.

bd.meaning: Because of that, customers reacted badly to Ferrari's first electric car.
chunks: customers reacted badly (mal = badly, sits after 'ont')
à la première voiture électrique de Ferrari
bd.key: “mal” + past participle = “badly ___ed.” Small adverbs like mal slot in right after the helper verb, before the past participle.

body.fr: Dans la finance, les banques utilisent des {{titres compliqués|complicated titles}} pour cacher la perte de statut de leurs employés.

bd.meaning: In finance, banks use complicated titles to hide their employees' loss of status.
chunks: Dans la finance, les banques utilisent
la perte de statut de leurs employés
bd.key: pour + plain verb, yet again. pour cacher = “to hide” — by now you can spot this pattern anywhere.

body.fr: Par exemple, chez Goldman Sachs, le titre de « {{partenaire|partner}} » existe encore, même si la banque n'est plus une vraie société de partenaires.

bd.meaning: For example, at Goldman Sachs, the title of 'partner' still exists, even though the bank is no longer really a partnership.
chunks: for example, at Goldman Sachs (chez = at the place/company of)
le titre de « partenaire » existe encore
la banque n'est plus une vraie société de partenaires
the bank is no longer really a partnership (ne...plus = no longer)
bd.key: ne … plus = “no longer / not anymore.” A cousin of ne … pas — same sandwich shape, different meaning.

body.fr: La Silicon Valley se présente comme un endroit {{sans hiérarchie|without hierarchy}}.

bd.meaning: Silicon Valley presents itself as a place without hierarchy.
chunks: La Silicon Valley se présente comme
a place without hierarchy (sans = without, no article after it)
bd.key: “sans” drops the article, again. sans hiérarchie = “without hierarchy” — same rule as sans avocat and sans réponse.

body.fr: Mais en réalité, ses employés ont très peur que l'intelligence artificielle {{remplace|replace}} leur travail.

bd.meaning: But in reality, its employees are very afraid that AI will replace their jobs.
chunks: ses employés ont très peur que
its employees are very afraid that
bd.key: avoir peur que + verb = “to be afraid that ___.” A useful pattern for expressing worry about something happening.

body.fr: Le président Donald Trump illustre bien cette {{peur du statut perdu|fear of lost status}}.

bd.meaning: President Donald Trump illustrates this fear of lost status well.
chunks: Le président Donald Trump illustre bien
bd.key: Past participle as adjective: perdu (lost, from perdre) describes “statut” just like a regular adjective — many past participles work this way.

body.fr: Il attaque souvent les universités et les médias, {{deux institutions|two institutions}} qui donnent normalement du prestige.

bd.meaning: He often attacks universities and the media, two institutions that normally give prestige.
chunks: two institutions that normally give (qui = that/which)
bd.key: “qui” hooks on more description, as before: “two institutions THAT normally give prestige.”

body.fr: Mais un jour, il {{va quitter|is going to leave}} son poste, et il va perdre beaucoup de statut.

bd.meaning: But one day, he's going to leave his position, and he's going to lose a lot of status.
chunks: he's going to leave his position (aller + plain verb)
bd.key: aller + plain verb = the future, twice in one sentence. va quitter and va perdre both use the same “aller + plain verb” shape.

body.fr: Heureusement, la peur de perdre son statut n'est pas seulement {{négative|negative}}.

bd.meaning: Fortunately, the fear of losing your status isn't only negative.
chunks: la peur de perdre son statut
the fear of losing one's status
bd.key: ne … pas seulement = “not only.” The negation sandwich wraps around “seulement” to soften a claim rather than deny it fully.

body.fr: Elle {{pousse|pushes, drives}} aussi les gens à changer de travail et à créer de nouvelles choses.

bd.meaning: It also drives people to change jobs and create new things.
chunks: Elle pousse aussi les gens à
et à créer de nouvelles choses
bd.key: pousser qqn à + plain verb = “to drive/push someone to ___.” Same shape as aider qqn à — a person, then à, then the plain verb.

body.fr: Le jeune banquier du début de cette histoire a finalement {{quitté|quit, left}} son emploi pour chercher plus d'argent, et surtout, plus de statut.

bd.meaning: The young banker from the start of this story finally quit his job to look for more money, and above all, more status.
chunks: Le jeune banquier du début de cette histoire
the young banker from the start of this story
finally quit his job (a...quitté = past form)
bd.key: Past = avoir + past participle, to close. a quitté = “quit” — the same pattern this story has used throughout to talk about what already happened.

grammar.fr: La banque n'est plus une société de partenaires
grammar.en: ne … plus = “no longer / not anymore.” Same sandwich shape as ne … pas, but it marks something that used to be true and isn't now.

grammar.fr: Elle pousse les gens à changer de travail
grammar.en: pousser / aider / apprendre qqn à + plain verb = “to get someone to ___.” A family of verbs that all use the same shape: person, then à, then a plain verb.
aller + plain verb = the near future. Only aller changes with the subject; the second verb stays plain. Your “future = aller + verb” key, again.

quiz.q: Pourquoi les marques de luxe comme LVMH perdent-elles leur statut ?
quiz.a: Parce qu'elles ont vendu leurs produits à trop de gens et ont perdu leur image exclusive. (Because they sold their products to too many people and lost their exclusive image.)

flag: This retells a witty Economist “Schumpeter” opinion column, so the compression is heavier than usual: I dropped the Hermès-tie anecdote, the front/middle/back-office bank hierarchy, Nike's leisurewear pivot, Knight Frank's luxury index, and the section on Trump's children striking business deals. la mort du statut is my own translation of the column's coined phrase “status death” — there's no established French equivalent, and a French writer covering the same idea might reach for déclassement (downgrading) instead. The original is opinionated and sardonic; I flattened the tone to stay neutral, as instructed.
